text:
Sam (AE): Heads up 11 NovusHealth pushed back on our standard order form. They want a 180k token/month POC credit for 90 days instead of a discount, want DocuSign to trigger services, and insist on strict BYOK (provider must not hold plaintext keys). Finance says PO before billing. Can we align?
Ivy (SE): We can do 180k/month credits applied as invoice credits. BYOK fine but must document limits - e.g., cache snapshotting requires provider-side unwrap unless they provide key agent on-host. I'll write a 1-page KMS appendix.
Ramon (Sales Ops): Finance requirement: PO before any billable activation. If customer insists DocuSign first, Ops recommends a sandbox-only activation until PO is received. We should add a billing-contingency clause.
Hannah (Legal): We avoid touching the MSA SLA values. For short POCs we typically create an addendum: POC term 90 days, temporary SLA (only if customer requests) noted as 99.5% in addendum, liability limited to fees paid during POC, and PO contingency language. Also include a BYOK appendix clarifying provider has no key access and the tradeoffs on features.
Sam (AE): Customer redline pasted below. They propose: ```
- POC credits: 180,000 tokens per month for months 1-3; applied as invoice credit
- Commencement: services begin upon countersignature; PO to follow within 7 days
- KMS: Customer-managed keys (provider may not access plaintext keys)
- Overage: billed at 50% of list until credits exhausted
```
Ivy (SE): 50% of list for overage is ok for a limited POC. Need explicit meter definition: "Token units measured on a per-UTC-month basis using Provider billing meter." Also add a short example for clarity.
Ramon (Sales Ops): DocuSign template ord-poc-std supports addenda and parallel signing. My suggested flow: customer uploads PO -> we ingest and verify -> send DocuSign envelope with addendum attached -> customer legal + procurement sign in parallel -> provider signs last. If they sign before PO, envelope will include a PO placeholder and the order form will contain this contingency: "Commencement of billable services is contingent upon receipt of an authorized purchase order within 14 days of countersignature; Provider may suspend billable services if PO not received."
contract-bot: Note: template ord-poc-std available. Template ID: tmpl-ord-std-3. Use tags: po_num, credit_amt, poc_term.
Hannah (Legal): Draft contingency language acceptable. Also add POC termination clause allowing either party to terminate on 7 days' notice during the POC, and a liability cap equal to fees paid during the POC term. I'll upload addendum draft to shared drive.
Sam (AE): Customer replied: they prefer a 7-day PO window. Finance will not accept <14 days without exec approval. If they insist, escalate.
Ramon (Sales Ops): Requesting PO exception requires revenue ops signoff. @Sam capture if customer can sign procurement in parallel to speed it up.
Sam (AE): They can sign procurement in parallel; they're going to upload PO today. I'll update when it's in.
contract-bot: Action logged: prepared envelope draft env-13077 using tmpl-ord-std-3. Waiting for PO to autofill.
Ramon (Sales Ops): PO 49077022 uploaded and pasted into envelope. Sending for signatures now. Routing: cust_legal + cust_proc parallel -> cust_eng -> provider_ae -> provider_finance(visibility).
Hannah (Legal): Final redlines accepted with addendum and contingency clause. Countersign after customer completes.
Ramon (Sales Ops): Envelope completed and countersigned. Sandbox activated pending KMS handoff.
Ivy (SE): KMS handoff scheduled next Tue. I'll post the short tech appendix and an internal checklist to the thread after the call.
Sam (AE): Closing loop: POC started, credits set on billing template, KMS handoff scheduled. Thanks team! :white_check_mark:
